title: Multi-hop fallback choreography for pinned model versions with soft-deprecation quarantines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers can pin model versions to ensure stable outputs, but when a pinned variant becomes overloaded, deprecated, or unavailable in a region there is no expressive, auditable choreography that balances availability, latency, and correctness. Current fallbacks are single-step and opaque to customers, which causes unpredictable routing and poor operator visibility.

Goal: Implement a multi-hop fallback choreography and 'soft-deprecation quarantine' mechanism for pinned versions that: (1) preserves regional affinity where possible, (2) prefers model-variant compatibility using published performance profiles, (3) exposes fallback decisioning in audit logs and the Console, and (4) supports an operator-controlled quarantine window during which deprecated pins can be auto-evicted without immediate user-facing breakage.

Scope: runtime routing policy updates, routing graph representation, fallback scoring by (compatibility, latency delta, cost delta, regional proximity), console UI for pin-state and quarantine visualization, telemetry/alerts for fallback churn and quarantine evictions, and documentation for onboarding teams and customers.
acceptance_criteria: Routing engine supports ordered multi-hop fallbacks for pinned versions with a configurable max-hops (default 3)
Fallback decisions score candidates using model compatibility (tokenization/schema), published performance profiles, region proximity, and cost priorities
Soft-deprecation quarantine exists: deprecated pins enter a quarantined state for a configurable window (default 72h) during which traffic is gradually shifted to fallback candidates before eviction
Console surfaces pin health, active fallback path with scores, and quarantine timeline; customers can opt into automatic eviction or manual approval
Audit logs record each fallback event with reason, selected candidate, score components, and the performance profile used for the decision
End-to-end integration tests covering regional outage, overloaded variant, and performance-regression scenarios pass
Telemetry emits metrics: fallback_rate_by_pin, fallback_latency_overhead, quarantine_evictions, and fallback_churn_alerts
SLOs: 99th percentile routing decision latency < 50ms added to request path, and fallback-related errors accounted in existing errors metrics
tasks: Design: write fallback choreography spec and sequence diagrams (design doc link below)
Runtime: implement fallback graph traversal with scoring hooks and max-hops enforcement
Routing: add region-aware candidate filter and performance-profile lookup in routing decision path
Console: UI card showing pin status, active fallback chain, quarantine countdown, and manual eviction control
Telemetry: add metrics and tracing spans for decision inputs and outputs
API: extend pin API to accept quarantine policy fields and fallback preference (latency/cost/compatibility)
E2E tests: simulate region failover, high-latency variant, and deprecation rollout with quarantine enabled
Docs: update onboarding guide and performance profile publishing docs to describe interaction with fallback orchestration
design_notes: We will treat published performance profiles as first-class inputs to scoring: normalized latency and token-cost deltas are weighted against compatibility and regional proximity
Quarantine is a soft state: traffic shifts conservatively using a decay factor (e.g., 20% per hour) during the quarantine window; final eviction requires either expiry or manual approval
To avoid cascading failures, fallback decisions will prefer variants with identical tokenizers and response-shape compatibility. If none exist, degrade to best-effort but annotate the audit log
Fallback scoring weights will be configurable at org and pin level. Default weights: compatibility 40%, latency delta 30%, regional proximity 20%, cost 10%
We intentionally avoid changing the token-serving runtime to keep per-token execution identical; routing changes only change destination selection
Routing latency budget: decision computation should be <50ms and executed asynchronously where possible; synchronous path only when required for correctness
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Internal rollout for redwood-internal orgs with quarantine enabled and max-hops=2
Phase 2 (beta): Early customer opt-in for Dedicated customers; collect telemetry for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (default): Turn on for all new pins with default quarantine policy; notify customers via Console and changelog
Phase 4: Retro-fit older pins in 'legacy' state with admin notification and opt-in automation
Rollback: global feature flag to disable multi-hop choreography and revert to single-step fallback immediately
monitoring_and_alerting: Create Grafana dashboard: Pin health board (fallback_rate_by_pin, fallback_latency_overhead, quarantine_evictions)
Alert: fallback_churn_alert when a single pin has >100 fallback events in 1h
Alert: quarantine_eviction_spike when evictions > 5x baseline in 1h
Tracing: add tags to traces showing fallback_path and applied_scores for postmortems
SLI: routing-decision-latency p99 < 50ms (track and alert if breached)
Oncall runbook: steps to validate routing decisions, manually evict/restore pins, and toggle feature flag
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring components with mocked performance profiles
Integration tests for routing engine with simulated regional topologies
Load tests to validate decision latency under high QPS and ensure max-hops enforcement
Chaos test: induce regional network partitions and verify quarantine decay shifts traffic gradually
Customer simulation: replay production request mix for a pinned model and assert graceful degradation
